standard_prerequisites.name: Integration of polynomials with rational coefficients
standard_prerequisites.use: The homotopy uses the unique polynomial $\int g'$ with vanishing constant term whose derivative is $g'$, which exists because $R$ contains $\mathbf{Q}$.

core_obligations: Reduce to the affine local statement that $\Omega^\bullet_{A/R} \to \Omega^\bullet_{A[t]/R}$ is a quasi-isomorphism of complexes of $R$-modules, for an $R$-algebra $A$ with $R$ a $\mathbf{Q}$-algebra (proof lines 1535-1540).
Exhibit the homotopy inverse sending $g\omega + g'\mathrm{d}t \wedge \omega'$ to $g(0)\omega$ (proof lines 1540-1543).

Exhibit the homotopy sending the same element to $(\int g')\omega'$, using that $R$ contains the rationals for the integration of polynomials, and conclude the quasi-isomorphism and the identification of de Rham cohomology (proof lines 1543-1548).
proof_roadmap: The homotopy and the use of the rationals (proof lines 1543-1548).
difficulty_reason: The lemma shows that over a base containing the rationals the de Rham complex of a line bundle is quasi-isomorphic to the pullback of that of the base, so the de Rham cohomology does not change (statement lines 1527-1532). The proof reduces to the affine statement for a polynomial algebra, where it writes down an explicit homotopy inverse and homotopy, the latter using integration of polynomials with rational coefficients. The explicit homotopy is the substance, so the claim is H2.
